title: It-Cleft 強調句
titleEn: Using the It-cleft to emphasise a person, thing, time, place, reason or method

omissions: English versions of Chinese-only Important Rules are faithful editorial translations.

formula: It + is / was + person + who + clause

formulas.formula: It + is / was + person + who + clause

formulas.labelZh: 強調事物、時間、地點、原因或方法
formulas.formula: It + is / was + focused element + that + clause

example: It was John who saved me in the fire.
exampleZh: 在火災中救了我的正是約翰。

examples.en: It was John who saved me in the fire.
examples.zh: 在火災中救了我的正是約翰。
examples.highlight: It was John who saved me in the fire.

examples.en: It was yesterday that John called me.
examples.zh: 約翰正是在昨天致電給我。
examples.highlight: It was yesterday that John called me.

examples.en: It was at the station that we met.
examples.highlight: It was at the station that we met.

rules.zh: 現在的事情一般使用 is；過去的事情一般使用 was。
rules.en: Use is for present situations and was for past situations. It is Mary who prepares the reports. It was Mary who prepared the report yesterday.
examples: It is Mary who prepares the reports.
It was Mary who prepared the report yesterday.

rules.zh: 強調人物時，本練習使用 who。
rules.en: Use who when the focused element is a person. It was Ben who opened the door.
examples: It was Ben who opened the door.

rules.zh: 強調事物、時間、地點、原因或方法時，使用 that。
rules.en: Use that for things, times, places, reasons and methods. It was the red bag that she bought. It was on Monday that we met. It was at school that the accident happened. It was because he was ill that he stayed home.
examples: It was the red bag that she bought.
It was on Monday that we met.
It was at school that the accident happened.
It was because he was ill that he stayed home.

rules.zh: 改寫後必須保留原句的時態和意思。
rules.en: Keep the original tense and meaning. Amy found the key. It was Amy who found the key. Amy checks the door every night. It is Amy who checks the door every night.
examples: Amy found the key.
It was Amy who found the key.
Amy checks the door every night.
It is Amy who checks the door every night.

rules.zh: 不要在答案中加入原句沒有提供的新資料。
rules.en: The focused information must already appear in the source sentence.
examples: The focused information must already appear in the source sentence.

rules.zh: 以下句子並不是本課所學的 It-cleft 強調句：
rules.en: Not every sentence beginning with It is or It was is an It-cleft sentence. It is raining. It is important that you arrive early. It was difficult to understand the instructions.
examples: Not every sentence beginning with It is or It was is an It-cleft sentence.
It is raining.
It is important that you arrive early.
It was difficult to understand the instructions.

benefits.zh: 這個句型能立即告訴聽者或讀者，句子中哪個人物、事物或細節最重要。 第二句清楚強調救人的人是 John，而不是其他人。
benefits.en: It makes the most important information clear. This structure immediately tells the listener or reader which person, thing or detail is especially important. Compare: John saved me in the fire. It was John who saved me in the fire.
examples: It makes the most important information clear.
It was John who saved me in the fire.

benefits.zh: 你可以使用 It-cleft 句糾正錯誤資料，清楚指出真正正確的人物或細節。 （會議是在星期一，而不是星期二舉行的。）
benefits.en: It helps you correct a misunderstanding. You can use an It-cleft sentence to show that one detail is correct and another is not. It was Monday, not Tuesday, that the meeting took place.
examples: It helps you correct a misunderstanding.
You can use an It-cleft sentence to show that one detail is correct and another is not.
It was Monday, not Tuesday, that the meeting took place.

benefits.zh: It-cleft 句很適合用來回答 who、what、when、where、why 或 how 問題。
benefits.en: It gives direct answers to important questions. It-cleft sentences are useful when answering questions beginning with who, what, when, where, why or how. It-cleft Who found the wallet? It was Nina who found it.
examples: It gives direct answers to important questions.
Who found the wallet?
It was Nina who found it.

benefits.zh: 事件本身沒有改變，但你可以選擇希望聽者特別留意哪一部分。
benefits.en: It changes the emphasis without changing the basic facts. The event remains the same, but you can choose which part the listener should notice. It was Nina who found the wallet. It was the wallet that Nina found. It was at the station that Nina found the wallet.
examples: It changes the emphasis without changing the basic facts.
The event remains the same, but you can choose which part the listener should notice.
It was Nina who found the wallet.
It was the wallet that Nina found.
It was at the station that Nina found the wallet.

benefits.zh: 除了經常使用普通的主語開頭外，你也可以使用 It-cleft 句突出重點，令口語和寫作的句式更有變 化。
benefits.en: It gives your speaking and writing more sentence variety. Instead of always beginning with an ordinary subject, you can use an It-cleft sentence to present an important point more effectively.
examples: It gives your speaking and writing more sentence variety.

sourceOmissions: English versions of Chinese-only Important Rules are faithful editorial translations.
